baseline: R. Campbell Thompson, The Epic of Gilgamish: a new translation from a collation of the cuneiform tablets in the British Museum rendered literally into English hexameters, London: Luzac & Co., 1928 (archive.org thompson-1928-gilgamesh)

sources.TH-A: Thompson 1928, his translation of the Assyrian (Nineveh, 7th c. BC) version
sources.TH-OB: Thompson 1928, his translation of Old Babylonian tablets he interpolates (Pennsylvania and Yale tablets in Tablets II-III; Berlin/Meissner tablet in Tablets IX-X)
sources.TH-A+OB: Thompson 1928, Assyrian text restored in part from the Old Babylonian (his note, p. 20)
sources.TH-BOG: Thompson 1928, printed note translating an Akkadian fragment from Boghaz Keui (cuneiform text published by Weidner, KUB IV 12)
sources.TH-HIT: Thompson 1928, English of the Hittite version; Thompson credits 'Translation from J. Friedrich, Alter Orient 25, 2, 31, and Ungnad, Kulturfragen 4-5, 20' (p. 31) and 'Translation by Friedrich, and Ungnad' (p. 36). RIGHTS FLAG.

conventions: Every original-en paragraph is Thompson's own printed text; no other translator's words are used anywhere.
Verse lines are joined with single spaces (no embedded newlines); paragraph breaks follow Thompson's section headings, column breaks and sense blocks.
Kept as printed: Thompson's wording, spelling, name forms (Gilgamish, Erech, Uta-Napishtim, Ur-Shanabi, Nin-sun), round-bracket amplifications, (?) marks, accents (removéd), quotation marks.

Normalised typography: restoration half-brackets and square brackets removed (restored words kept); footnote numbers and line numbers removed; runs of gap dots printed as ' . . . '; Thompson's italic section headings omitted (recorded in locators).

Thompson's own Addenda et Corrigenda applied: p.11 l.48 '(and)'; p.22 l.5 '(forsooth),'; p.22 l.21 'friend'; p.27 l.46 'Nippur'; p.31 l.3 'seven mutilated'; p.18 l.14 dash deleted. (p.15 bracket and p.51 footnote-number corrections are moot after bracket/footnote removal.)

Thompson's italic editorial notes are kept in original-en only where they print translated lines (5 paragraphs, kind=thompson-printed-note-with-translated-lines); purely descriptive gap notes are recorded in the locator field instead.

modern-en and modern-da are fresh renderings aligned 1:1 with original-en; no brackets, asterisks or (?) marks; lacunae end at the gap (em dash) or use a short bridge only where Thompson's surviving text or note makes the meaning plain.
